final_message:
empty `order_id` 5, bad `unit_price` 4, bad `currency` 4, bad `updated_at` 4 |
| Valid | 1801 |
| Distinct order ids | 1445, so 1801 − 1445 = **356** duplicates removed |
| Cancelled / test / included | 191 / 362 / **892** (191 + 362 + 892 = 1445) |
| Refund rows | 159: 5 repeated ids, 123 matched, 31 ignored (6 unknown order ids, 25 pointing at cancelled or test orders), 0 unreadable |
| Gross / refunds (USD) | 117,375.98 / 9,616.98, a rate of 0.0819 |

All the counts add up. Seven included orders have negative net revenue, and 56 have a net of 0 or less at cents; those don't count toward paying customers on their own. Six refunds are dated 2026 and still count. Three of the kept order versions have a 2026 `updated_at`.

## Decisions where the README was silent, and how many rows each affected
- **Strict whitespace:** 0 rows rejected. Surrounding spaces only occur in `currency`, where trimming is allowed.
- **Email domain:** the text after the last `@` must equal `test.shopco.io` exactly, ignoring case. 4 rows on `latest.shopco.io` stay real customers, and there are no subdomains of `test.shopco.io`.
- **Same `updated_at` instant:** the version read last wins. 0 ties in this export (my test data covers one).
- **Unreadable refund rows:** skipped and not counted as malformed. 0 in this export.
- **Repeated refund ids:** only the first is kept. 5 rows dropped.
- **No cap on refunds:** 7 orders end up with negative net revenue.
- **Quarter keys:** `2025-Q1` to `Q4` are always present. Every included order is dated 2025, so no extra keys were added.
- **Top product tie:** alphabetically first wins. Not needed here.

## Data the README didn't cover
- **Unexpected values:** `order_date` values `n/a` and `yesterday`, `updated_at` values `soon` and blank, currency `EURO`, quantity `n/a` and unit prices `12,99x` and blank. All are treated as malformed under the existing rules.
- **Rows with 11 fields:** treated as malformed under the field-count rule.
- **Other `is_test` values:** none outside the listed true and false values. `false`, `FALSE` and blank count as not test.
- **Two blank lines in each order file:** skipped, and not counted as rows or as malformed.

**My test data:** about 22 rows across three files, one of them with reordered columns, plus 7 refunds. It covers every malformed rule, a blank line, names containing commas, and a three-version duplicate where only the UTC offset picks the right winner (comparing as text would pick the wrong one). It also covers each test-account mark next to `Tester`/`Testa`, a tie, a repeated refund id, refunds to unknown and cancelled orders, an unreadable refund amount, a fully refunded customer and an even count for the median. The output matched answers I worked out by hand before running it.

The debug output only appears when you set `REPORT_DEBUG=1`. Everything is calculated exactly and rounded only at the end; the one exception is the cents rounding in the paying-customer test, as the README requires.
